name: Washington

agency.name: Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife

overview: WDFW draws special hunt permits for deer, elk, moose, bighorn sheep, mountain goat and fall turkey with a weighted-point system: each application earns one point in that category, points build while you are unsuccessful, and they reset to zero when you are drawn. Applicants rank up to four hunt choices per category (two in Quality deer and elk); the 2026 submission period ran April 20 - May 27, 2026 (extended by WDFW from May 20), with results by the end of June, and 2027 applications go on sale December 1, 2026. Residents and nonresidents compete in the same drawing; general deer, elk, black bear and cougar seasons use licenses and tags sold over the counter, and multi-season deer and elk tags are drawn separately.

species.residentNote: Residents and nonresidents enter the same drawing; WDFW publishes one combined count per hunt (no resident/nonresident split).
species.nonresidentNote: Nonresident special permit application: $152.30 per category (resident $9.61; Quality categories $18.72).
species.drawSystemSummary: WDFW issues special hunt permits through a weighted-point drawing: each application earns one point in that species category, points accumulate while unsuccessful, and they reset to zero when drawn (WAC 220-412-080). WDFW does not publish the weighting formula in the pamphlet or WAC. Applicants may list up to four hunt choices per category (two in Quality deer and elk). Elk special permit categories: Quality Elk, Bull Elk, Antlerless Elk, Youth, Hunters 65 and Over, Disabled Hunters and Master Hunters.
species.otcSummary: Elk licenses and general-season transport tags are sold over the counter; multi-season elk tags (1,000 for 2027) are drawn separately.

coverage.notes: Spring black bear special permits only (2020-2021); no spring permit season has been offered since. Fall bear is a general season. Per-hunt counts are WDFW's: 2020 and 2022-2025 'Total Applicants' and 'Permits Issued' from WDFW's game harvest reports; 2021 from WDFW's drawing summary (Power BI; applicants match the 2021 harvest report in all 934 matched hunts, while the harvest report's 'Permits Issued' is lower in 253 hunts, i.e. permits returned after the draw); 2026 = permits (quota) from the 2026 pamphlet only, because WDFW has not published 2026 applicant counts. Counts include every hunt choice position (1st-4th). Odds are computed as permits issued / applicants and do not reflect points. WDFW does not publish applicants by point level for these years, so byPoints and minPoints are omitted; the pamphlet's 'APPS/AVG POINTS' figures (average points of drawn applicants, rounded; verified equal to the 2021 drawing summary's 'Average Winner Points') are quoted in row notes, attached only when the next pamphlet lists the same hunt (same code, name, unit, legal animal, tag and category). For 2021 those APPS figures equal the drawing summary's applications in 614 of 616 hunts; for 2022-2025 they are lower than the harvest report's 'Total Applicants' (median ratio 0.98 for 2022 and about 0.93 for 2023-2025, hunts with 50+ applicants), a difference WDFW does not explain. Quotas for deer and elk come from that year's pamphlet; moose, sheep and goat quotas from the harvest report. The 2024 drawing had a vendor allocation error that WDFW corrected by re-allocating and adding permits.

WDFW does not publish applicants by point level for these years, so byPoints and minPoints are omitted; the pamphlet's 'APPS/AVG POINTS' figures (average points of drawn applicants, rounded; verified equal to the 2021 drawing summary's 'Average Winner Points') are quoted in row notes, attached only when the next pamphlet lists the same hunt (same code, name, unit, legal animal, tag and category). For 2021 those APPS figures equal the drawing summary's applications in 614 of 616 hunts; for 2022-2025 they are lower than the harvest report's 'Total Applicants' (median ratio 0.98 for 2022 and about 0.93 for 2023-2025, hunts with 50+ applicants), a difference WDFW does not explain. Quotas for deer and elk come from that year's pamphlet; moose, sheep and goat quotas from the harvest report. The 2024 drawing had a vendor allocation error that WDFW corrected by re-allocating and adding permits.
No draw: cougar is a general (over-the-counter) season with harvest caps.
